model_annotation: The figure presents a line plot illustrating the co-occurrence number of biomedical knowledge, denoted as $|D(s, o)|$, across different groups of large language models (LLMs) on the ClicKT dataset. The x-axis represents the co-occurrence number, scaled logarithmically from $10^1$ to $10^3$, with tick marks at each order of magnitude. The y-axis represents the percentage of LLMs, scaled linearly from 55 to 65. The plot compares five groups: Base (black, solid line), ROME (blue, dashed line), FT (green, dash-dot line), MEMIT (red, dotted line), and NEMIT (purple, dash-dot-dot line). The Base group shows a steady increase from approximately 55% to 65% as the co-occurrence number increases. The ROME group shows a similar trend, starting at about 55% and rising to 65%. The FT group starts at 55% and increases to 65%. The MEMIT group starts at 55% and rises to 65%. The NEMIT group starts at 55% and increases to 65%. The legend indicates that the groups are categorized based on their pre-training method, with the Base group being the original model, ROME being a fine-tuned model, FT being a fine-tuned model with a different training set, MEMIT being a model trained with a different method, and NEMIT being a model trained with a different method. The plot shows that as the co-occurrence number increases, the percentage of LLMs in each group also increases, with the Base group showing the highest percentage at all co-occurrence numbers.
